rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: RBA 4.85% (Nov 3, 6–3); BoE Nov 5 hike to 4.00% ~94%; Fed Dec hike ~79% (from ~74%); BoC Dec ~56% (from ~45%); ECB Dec ~86%; BoJ Dec ~80%
rows.read: Most big central banks still lean toward higher rates, and strong US jobs figures made a December Fed hike look more likely. Canada’s central bank repeated that more rises may be needed, while Australia’s looks ready to pause after its latest hike. Currencies are moving on hints about the next step, not the hikes already made.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US job openings 7.52M Sep (fcst 7.11M); US factory orders +1.8% Sep (fcst +1.2%); US ISM manufacturing 55.5 Oct; dairy auction +3.0%
rows.read: The US economy keeps surprising on the strong side, with more open jobs and busier factories than expected. That gives the Federal Reserve room to keep raising rates and supports the dollar. Canada and Australia remain the soft spots.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Swiss CPI 1.5% y/y Oct (fcst 1.3%), core 0.5%; Brent ~$104.68; euro-area flash CPI Nov 4: forecast 4.0%
rows.read: Fuel is still pushing prices up almost everywhere, even in Switzerland, where inflation had been very low. Underlying prices there stayed calm, so the jump says more about energy than about a broad rise. Euro-area figures on Wednesday are the week’s main inflation check.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: DXY ~101.86; limited US strikes on Qeshm Island; Iran says it downed a US drone; US 10Y touched ~4.97%; USD/JPY ~158.46
rows.read: Markets stayed calm on US midterm election day, even as US and Iranian forces clashed near the Strait of Hormuz. Investors are betting the peace talks carry on, so the safe-haven currencies got little extra lift. Rising US yields, not fear, drove the biggest move, a weaker yen.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$104.68, WTI ~$96.58 at the NY close (London highs ~$106.61 / ~$98.06); dairy auction index +3.0%
rows.read: Oil ended near Monday’s lower level after an early bounce faded, so exporters like Canada still have less support than a week ago and importers like Japan and the euro area a smaller bill. Iran’s offer to reopen Hormuz quickly shows how fast prices could fall on a deal. Firm dairy prices helped New Zealand.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 27: funds strongly against CAD, against EUR (real money for), against NZD, for AUD (real money strongly against), strongly for gold (cut); oil net long among weakest since 2015
rows.read: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, and they are also betting against the euro and the kiwi, while real money investors bet for the euro. Their large bets on gold have been shrinking. New figures arrive Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: Fitch: France A+, outlook negative (Oct 30); Moody’s Aa3 negative; Canada federal budget Nov 5, 3:00 PM CT
rows.read: Debt worries in France, where two rating firms have a negative outlook, keep a weight on the euro. Canada presents its federal budget on Thursday, and a big rise in borrowing would weigh on the loonie.
